extra_audio.text: That is a fair question, and I want to be precise. Based on our current pipeline, we expect revenue in the range of ninety to one hundred million. These are preliminary numbers, and they are subject to two contracts we are still negotiating. The data suggests that the banking sector will continue to grow. So I would treat the top of the range as indicative, not as a promise. Let's leave room for an update after the second quarter.

I have negotiated with founders for fifteen years, and I write down every number they say. If a founder tells me revenue will be one hundred million next year, I will ask for it again in twelve months. The founders I trust give me the number with its limits. Based on our pipeline, roughly ninety to one hundred, subject to two contracts. That is not weak. That tells me he knows exactly where the risk is.

In my first negotiation, I wanted to sound confident, so I gave the buyer a firm number for the next year. We missed it by eight percent. It was a good year, but the buyer used that eight percent to cut the earnout. In my second deal, I said: based on our current numbers, we expect growth in the range of fifteen to twenty percent, and I would treat the top of the range as indicative. We hit seventeen, and nobody said a word.
